**CC2_F003: WITHDRAW.** The schema flagged this as a near-duplicate (cosine 0.72 to Gemini_UNSTRUCTURED) with admissibility failures. On re-examination, the root cause overlaps with C0004 (unanchored gate-status matching). Withdrawing as independent discovery.

## Verdicts on Existing Findings

CONFIRM C0012 — The marker regex permits Markdown headers (`#{1,6}`) but the `section_terminator` (line 80–85) lacks the equivalent `(?:#{1,6}\s*)?` prefix. A next-section header like `### NOVELTY:` will not fire the terminator, causing block overrun. The fix proposed in C0012 is correct and sufficient.

CONFIRM C0013 — The `section_terminator` uses only `re.MULTILINE` (line 85) while the `marker_match` uses `re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE` (line 61). A model writing `Novelty:` or `verified:` in mixed/lowercase as a section header will not terminate the block. Confirmed independently by inspecting line 85 vs line 61.

CONFIRM C0016 — `σ_measured: N/A` is accepted unconditionally (lines 119–120) regardless of whether the finding contains a proposed fix. Per §15, N/A is only valid when no fix was proposed and no post-fix measurement is applicable. The parser needs the `finding_text` context to validate this.

## New Finding

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.45
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.65
FIND: `parse_admissibility_block` returns `list(ADMISSIBILITY_GATES)` (all 5 gate names) for two semantically distinct failure states: (1) the ADMISSIBILITY block is entirely missing from the finding text (line 64), and (2) the block IS present but every gate within it reports FAIL or is unmentioned. The caller receives the same `["S_min", "G-completeness", "d_tool", "σ_measured", "q_retest"]` output in both cases and cannot distinguish between them.

FOLLOW: The caller is `_feedback.py`'s feedback channel, which generates §17 corrective messages. Per §17, "block missing" should produce "ADMISSIBILITY FAIL: [...] (see §15)" telling the model to *supply the block*. "All gates failed within a present block" should tell the model to *fix each gate's evidence*. With the current API, the caller cannot generate appropriately differentiated feedback. The consequence is suboptimal corrective signal — models that attempted the block but failed every gate receive the same feedback as models that omitted it entirely, reducing the feedback channel's corrective precision. In practice this affects convergence speed (more rounds to fix) rather than correctness (the model must still fix all 5 gates either way).

ANALYSE: SOFT constraint. The downstream action is the same in both cases (model must supply/fix all gates). The distinction is quality-of-feedback, not correctness-of-gating. The function's docstring (line 37) documents this intentionally. CONFIRMED as a design limitation with bounded consequence.

FIX: Change return type to carry a boolean indicating whether the block was found. Minimal disruption — callers that destructure get the list; callers that need the distinction check the flag.

FALSIFICATION:
  FALSIFIER: The ambiguity does not actually affect downstream behaviour — if the caller's action is identical in both cases, the finding is a style preference, not a functional defect.
  ATTEMPT: Examined §17 operational directive for whether "block missing" and "all gates failed" require different corrective actions. §17 says "either supply the missing block in full or withdraw the finding" — which applies equally to both states. However, §17 also says feedback should be *per-gate* ("If one or more §15 gates [...] failed") which implies the feedback channel knows WHICH gates failed and WHY. A present-but-all-failed block has per-gate failure reasons; a missing block has none. The corrective text should differ.
  RESULT: Claim holds. The distinction is load-bearing for feedback quality even though both paths require the model to supply all 5 gates. The fix is backward-compatible (opt-in keyword argument), so it cannot break existing callers.
  FIX FALSIFICATION: Could the new keyword argument break existing callers? No — default is `False`, preserving original return type. Type checkers may flag the union return type; addressed by using `@overload` if needed, but unnecessary for a PoC.
